questions.question: Define the Palaeolithic period [K] [2]
questions.solution_html:
• • Prehistoric era, "Old Stone Age."

  • • Hunter-gatherer lifestyle.

questions.question: Describe how early paintings inspire the evolution of alphabets and languages. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe how early paintings inspire the evolution of alphabets and languages. [K] / [CO2]
  • • Cave paintings used symbolic visuals to express meaning.
  • • Pictorial signs gradually developed into pictograms.
  • • Example: Egyptian hieroglyphs evolving from symbolic drawings.
  • • These early symbols later transformed into phonetic writing systems.
  • • Helped structure communication into recognizable linguistic patterns

questions.question: Define the basic structure of a story. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Define the basic structure of a story. [U] / [CO1]

  • • Middle presents conflict or rising action.
  • • End resolves the conflict.
  • • Example: Most folk tales follow the three-act structure.

questions.question: Discuss how mesolithic art influenced early civilizations. / [CO2]

  • • Depicted hunting techniques and survival practices.
  • • Provided visual documentation of community life.
  • • Influenced early symbolic communication.
  • • Encouraged development of ritualistic traditions.
  • • Shaped cultural identity within groups.
  • • Example: Mesolithic rock art in India influencing early tribal rituals.
  • • Laid groundwork for structured art forms in later civilizations.

questions.question: Analyse how Roman epic bridges the oral and literary traditions of its civilization. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze how Roman epic bridges the oral and literary traditions of its civilization. [An] / [CO3]
  • • Borrowed narrative structures from earlier oral storytelling.
  • • Written form added permanence and sophistication.
  • • Blended mythological stories with historical events.
  • • Helped preserve cultural and political ideals.
  • • Reflected Roman values such as honour and duty.
  • • Example: Virgil’s Aeneid merging myth with state propaganda.
  • • Created a national literary identity.
